evidenceClaims.statement: Low chemistry total CO2 does not by itself distinguish metabolic acidification from a respiratory process; contemporaneous gas measurements help define the components.
evidenceClaims.limitation: R1.1 is expert opinion; no universal arterial-over-venous superiority claimed.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

evidenceClaims.statement: Albumin adjustment can reveal an anion burden hidden by low albumin; the cited relation is AG + 0.25 * (40 - albumin in g/L).
evidenceClaims.limitation: Conditional guideline; use the stated laboratory reference and units, not a universal normal gap.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

evidenceClaims.statement: An elevated albumin-adjusted gap supports looking for unmeasured acids even when gastrointestinal bicarbonate losses also exist.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single adequate guideline; lactate/ketones are offered initial tests, not an exhaustive or universally ordered algorithm.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

evidenceClaims.statement: For metabolic acidosis the cited expected arterial PCO2 is 1.5 * bicarbonate + 8, with a +/-2 mmHg range; a higher measured value supports an additional respiratory acidifying process.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Expert-opinion compensation estimate; arterial sampling and coherent paired values are required.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

evidenceClaims.statement: When metabolic acidemia is accompanied by inadequate respiratory compensation, ventilation and its reversible impairments need reassessment rather than accepting the gas as appropriate compensation.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single adequate guideline plus physiological application; no rate, volume, target or automatic intubation instruction is taught.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

evidenceClaims.statement: Residual infusate in catheter draws can distort electrolyte and blood-gas measurements through dilution.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One laboratory review; the numeric saline-mixture example is constructed arithmetic, not a validated contamination cutoff.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

evidenceClaims.statement: Simultaneous chemistry/gas disagreement should be reconciled with collection provenance before using the discrepant result to justify cause-specific treatment.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Independent synthesis of specimen-quality and acid-base sources; does not license delaying treatment in an unstable patient.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

evidenceClaims.statement: Paired carefully collected serum and lithium-heparin plasma potassium help assess suspected pseudohyperkalaemia; high platelets can raise serum potassium during clotting.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One guideline. Its serum-minus-plasma >0.4 mmol/L criterion concerns raised serum with normal plasma; an elevated plasma result must still be acted on.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

evidenceClaims.statement: The UKKA community pathway directs urgent hospital assessment when potassium is at least 6.5 mmol/L.
evidenceClaims.limitation: UK pathway, not a universal jurisdictional threshold; normal symptoms or ECG do not establish safety of confirmed severe potassium.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

evidenceClaims.statement: Calcium can improve hyperkalaemic electrical disturbance without lowering potassium; insulin-glucose shifts potassium, while a beta agonist is an adjunct in severe disease.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One guideline; overview and linked page show calcium-grade drift. No exact calcium regimen or outcome benefit asserted.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

evidenceClaims.statement: UKKA recommends additional glucose infusion after insulin-glucose when pretreatment glucose is below 7 mmol/L.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One guideline, UK hospital regimen. Dose, rate and monitoring times are not prescribed in the question.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

evidenceClaims.statement: Measured osmolality and glucose help separate hypotonic hyponatraemia from solute-related or analytical low sodium results.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Not all normal-osmolality low sodium is artifact; resolve the method and clinical context.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

evidenceClaims.statement: Urine concentration and sodium interpreted with volume findings help distinguish water retention from nonrenal salt/water losses.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single guideline; recent diuretics and renal dysfunction can invalidate simple urine-sodium inference.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

evidenceClaims.statement: Hypovolaemic hypotonic hyponatraemia is treated by restoring extracellular volume with isotonic crystalloid, with sodium/urine-output reassessment.
evidenceClaims.limitation: No exact volume/rate or correction target is prescribed; severe neurologic symptoms require a different acute pathway.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

evidenceClaims.statement: Restoring volume can suppress antidiuresis and produce water diuresis that accelerates sodium correction.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single guideline; observed urine/sodium trajectory establishes risk more directly than a fixed prediction.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

evidenceClaims.statement: Malnutrition and hypokalaemia increase osmotic-demyelination risk; high-risk correction exceeding 8 mmol/L in a day warrants urgent reassessment.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Guideline correction limits differ by risk group. No universal target or day-two limit inferred.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

evidenceClaims.statement: Established excessive correction may require stopping correction-driving treatment and specialist-directed electrolyte-free water and desmopressin.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single adequate guideline, very-low-certainty desmopressin evidence. Reactive rescue is distinguished from disputed proactive clamp use.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

evidenceClaims.statement: SIAD assessment requires hypotonicity with incompletely diluted urine, appropriate volume context and exclusion of adrenal, thyroid, renal and diuretic explanations.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single guideline; no diagnosis from urine sodium alone.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

evidenceClaims.statement: Water restriction is a usual initial treatment of stable SIAD without severe neurologic symptoms.
evidenceClaims.limitation: No exact fluid allowance or second-line drug ranking; guideline disagreement about vaptans is withheld.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

evidenceClaims.statement: An indirect sodium method can underestimate sodium in a high-solids sample; direct ISE testing helps resolve this interference.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One targeted laboratory review; the constructed lipid result is not an empirical interference threshold.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

evidenceClaims.statement: Hypotensive hypernatraemic patients may first require isotonic crystalloid to restore circulation before a separate water-deficit plan.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Narrative review plus older government guidance; no bolus size or correction speed is asserted.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

evidenceClaims.statement: Measured urinary electrolyte-free-water loss can be estimated as urine volume * [1 - (urine sodium + urine potassium)/plasma sodium].
evidenceClaims.limitation: One narrative review; retrospective measured estimate, not a prospective pump prescription. Include insensible/extrarenal losses separately.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

evidenceClaims.statement: Ongoing renal water losses must be considered separately from the initial water deficit when planning hypernatraemia replacement.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single adequate review; future losses change and require reassessment. No precise correction-rate rule.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

evidenceClaims.statement: Gastric acid losses can produce volume-depleted metabolic alkalosis with low urine chloride even when urinary sodium is higher.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single physiology review; urine chloride is interpreted before diuretics and saline alter the result.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

evidenceClaims.statement: Volume- and chloride-depleted metabolic alkalosis is treated with chloride-containing volume replacement and potassium chloride.
evidenceClaims.limitation: No exact dose/rate; treat the source of loss separately. Disease-specific obstruction management is outside this node.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

evidenceClaims.statement: Magnesium deficiency can sustain potassium wasting and an inadequate potassium-replacement response.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Government guidance corroborates checking/replacing magnesium in resistant hypokalaemia; no fixed replacement dose.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

evidenceClaims.statement: Marked symptomatic magnesium depletion may require monitored IV magnesium, with caution about repeated dosing during renal impairment.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One government source; no universal threshold, dose or infusion rate is taught.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

evidenceClaims.statement: Fluid reassessment includes oral/enteral intake and medication-carrier fluids; overload should prompt review of ongoing sodium and water administration.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single older government guidance; not a diuretic or renal replacement indication and not a weight-based maintenance formula.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

evidenceClaims.statement: In the 2024 adult DKA consensus, potassium below 3.5 mmol/L warrants replacement before insulin; insulin is delayed until potassium rises above 3.5 mmol/L.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single current multi-society consensus. Older pathways may use a different threshold; do not merge cutoffs.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

evidenceClaims.statement: The consensus defines DKA resolution by blood ketones below 0.6 mmol/L plus venous pH at least 7.3 or bicarbonate at least 18 mmol/L.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single consensus; the AND/OR relation matters. Glucose and electrolyte monitoring remain necessary.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

evidenceClaims.statement: Hyperchloraemic acidosis and persistent urinary ketones can outlast ketone clearance; neither anion gap nor urine ketones alone should define DKA resolution.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Urinary acetoacetate can increase as beta-hydroxybutyrate falls. No claim that every low bicarbonate after DKA is benign.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

evidenceClaims.statement: Transition from IV to subcutaneous insulin after resolution requires overlap to avoid an insulin-free interval.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single consensus; no dose or exact overlap duration is authored. Intake and prior basal insulin must be known.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

evidenceClaims.statement: Falling glucose does not establish DKA resolution; dextrose permits continued insulin when ketone acidosis persists.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Corroboration for historical frozen B2B30 only; no rewrite or new approval of it.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

evidenceClaims.statement: During HHS treatment sodium can rise as glucose falls; fluid changes should consider osmolality and volume response rather than sodium direction alone.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single consensus; hypotonic saline is considered when osmolality fails to fall despite adequate balance. No exact infusion rate is authored.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

evidenceClaims.statement: Ionized calcium reflects physiologically active calcium; total or albumin-adjusted calcium may not reliably represent it.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single government source; do not replace measurement with a new correction formula.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

evidenceClaims.statement: Prolonged air exposure can lower a gas sample PCO2, raise pH and reduce measured ionized calcium through increased protein binding.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One preanalytical review; no exact exposure-time or calcium-change formula claimed.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

evidenceClaims.statement: Symptomatic substantial hypocalcaemia can require monitored IV calcium gluconate rather than waiting for oral correction.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One government source; no exact drug dose, administration rate or extravasation technique authored.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

evidenceClaims.statement: Oral sodium chloride with a loop diuretic is one possible later-line SIAD approach after the initial water strategy.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single guideline; no universal ranking against urea or vaptans and no dose taught.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified constructed outside-hospital record.

evidenceClaims.statement: Acetazolamide promotes bicarbonate excretion but may increase potassium loss; volume/chloride depletion should be addressed in chloride-responsive alkalosis.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Narrative review; no fixed dose or universal use in volume-expanded patients.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified constructed outside-hospital record.

evidenceClaims.statement: Routine bicarbonate is not recommended in DKA; the 2024 consensus permits consideration when pH is below 7.0.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single consensus; no bicarbonate dose or universal prescription authored.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified constructed outside-hospital record.

evidenceClaims.statement: A basal-bolus subcutaneous regimen is preferred when transitioning suitable adults off IV insulin after DKA resolution.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single consensus; regimen depends on prior therapy, intake and clinical course. No correction-scale-only equivalence is inferred.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified constructed outside-hospital record.

evidenceClaims.statement: Urinary acidification studies are reserved for selected unexplained metabolic acidosis without unmeasured anions, with urine pH directed by suspicion of tubular acidosis.
evidenceClaims.limitation: R1.6-R1.7 are expert opinion; no urinary anion-gap formula or diagnostic cutoff is taught.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing the specified cause-directed acid-base evaluation.

evidenceClaims.statement: A recent diuretic can make urinary sodium difficult to use as a stand-alone marker of volume status in hypotonic hyponatraemia.
evidenceClaims.limitation: History, actual volume findings and renal context still matter; a high urine sodium alone does not establish SIAD or exclude depletion.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed review-response scenario.

evidenceClaims.statement: With chronic sodium at or below 120 mmol/L, advanced liver disease or severe hypokalaemia strengthens the case for considering relowering after a rise greater than 8 mmol/L within 24 hours.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Expert guideline interpretation and low-certainty rescue evidence. This does not justify relowering every patient starting above 120 or every transient sodium increase.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed review-response scenario.

evidenceClaims.statement: After excessive high-risk correction with ongoing water diuresis, specialist-directed free water and desmopressin can be used to reverse the rise and restrain further urinary water loss.
evidenceClaims.limitation: No dose or fixed monitoring interval prescribed; active relowering remains individualized. Both cited works discuss reactive/rescue use, separate from prophylactic clamp practice.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed review-response scenario.

evidenceClaims.statement: When the next DKA insulin plan is selected, ongoing ketonaemia/acidemia supports continued metabolic treatment, while potassium below the consensus boundary requires replacement and a safe repeat value before insulin is given.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Scoped application of the current potassium-delay and resolution recommendations to a new infusion-order review. No insulin dose, potassium dose or automatic pump action prescribed.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed review-response scenario.

evidenceClaims.statement: In adult HHS, the consensus limits glucose decline to no more than 5-6.7 mmol/L/hour and recommends an osmolality decline of 3-8 mOsm/kg/hour; fluid composition and infusion rate require separate assessment.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One current multi-society consensus. Constructed patient changes are observations, not a fixed pump prescription.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed review-response scenario.

evidenceClaims.statement: In metabolic acidosis, arterial CO2 below the expected compensatory range supports a concurrent respiratory alkalinizing process, whereas CO2 above it supports a concurrent respiratory acidifying process.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Compensation estimate and clinical application are expert-opinion physiology; no ventilator setting or specific cause is established by the gas alone.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed review-response scenario.

originalEvidenceClaims.statement: Low chemistry total CO2 does not by itself distinguish metabolic acidification from a respiratory process; contemporaneous gas measurements help define the components.
originalEvidenceClaims.limitation: R1.1 is expert opinion; no universal arterial-over-venous superiority claimed.
originalEvidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

originalEvidenceClaims.statement: Albumin adjustment can reveal an anion burden hidden by low albumin; the cited relation is AG + 0.25 * (40 - albumin in g/L).
originalEvidenceClaims.limitation: Conditional guideline; use the stated laboratory reference and units, not a universal normal gap.
originalEvidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

originalEvidenceClaims.statement: An elevated albumin-adjusted gap supports looking for unmeasured acids even when gastrointestinal bicarbonate losses also exist.
originalEvidenceClaims.limitation: Single adequate guideline; lactate/ketones are offered initial tests, not an exhaustive or universally ordered algorithm.
originalEvidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

originalEvidenceClaims.statement: For metabolic acidosis the cited expected arterial PCO2 is 1.5 * bicarbonate + 8, with a +/-2 mmHg range; a higher measured value supports an additional respiratory acidifying process.
originalEvidenceClaims.limitation: Expert-opinion compensation estimate; arterial sampling and coherent paired values are required.
originalEvidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

originalEvidenceClaims.statement: When metabolic acidemia is accompanied by inadequate respiratory compensation, ventilation and its reversible impairments need reassessment rather than accepting the gas as appropriate compensation.
originalEvidenceClaims.limitation: Single adequate guideline plus physiological application; no rate, volume, target or automatic intubation instruction is taught.
originalEvidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

originalEvidenceClaims.statement: Residual infusate in catheter draws can distort electrolyte and blood-gas measurements through dilution.
originalEvidenceClaims.limitation: One laboratory review; the numeric saline-mixture example is constructed arithmetic, not a validated contamination cutoff.
originalEvidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

originalEvidenceClaims.statement: Simultaneous chemistry/gas disagreement should be reconciled with collection provenance before using the discrepant result to justify cause-specific treatment.
originalEvidenceClaims.limitation: Independent synthesis of specimen-quality and acid-base sources; does not license delaying treatment in an unstable patient.
originalEvidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

originalEvidenceClaims.statement: Paired carefully collected serum and lithium-heparin plasma potassium help assess suspected pseudohyperkalaemia; high platelets can raise serum potassium during clotting.
originalEvidenceClaims.limitation: One guideline. Its serum-minus-plasma >0.4 mmol/L criterion concerns raised serum with normal plasma; an elevated plasma result must still be acted on.
originalEvidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

originalEvidenceClaims.statement: The UKKA community pathway directs urgent hospital assessment when potassium is at least 6.5 mmol/L.
originalEvidenceClaims.limitation: UK pathway, not a universal jurisdictional threshold; normal symptoms or ECG do not establish safety of confirmed severe potassium.
originalEvidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

originalEvidenceClaims.statement: Calcium can improve hyperkalaemic electrical disturbance without lowering potassium; insulin-glucose shifts potassium, while a beta agonist is an adjunct in severe disease.
originalEvidenceClaims.limitation: One guideline; overview and linked page show calcium-grade drift. No exact calcium regimen or outcome benefit asserted.
originalEvidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

originalEvidenceClaims.statement: UKKA recommends additional glucose infusion after insulin-glucose when pretreatment glucose is below 7 mmol/L.
originalEvidenceClaims.limitation: One guideline, UK hospital regimen. Dose, rate and monitoring times are not prescribed in the question.
originalEvidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

originalEvidenceClaims.statement: Measured osmolality and glucose help separate hypotonic hyponatraemia from solute-related or analytical low sodium results.
originalEvidenceClaims.limitation: Not all normal-osmolality low sodium is artifact; resolve the method and clinical context.
originalEvidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

originalEvidenceClaims.statement: Urine concentration and sodium interpreted with volume findings help distinguish water retention from nonrenal salt/water losses.
originalEvidenceClaims.limitation: Single guideline; recent diuretics and renal dysfunction can invalidate simple urine-sodium inference.
originalEvidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

originalEvidenceClaims.statement: Hypovolaemic hypotonic hyponatraemia is treated by restoring extracellular volume with isotonic crystalloid, with sodium/urine-output reassessment.
originalEvidenceClaims.limitation: No exact volume/rate or correction target is prescribed; severe neurologic symptoms require a different acute pathway.
originalEvidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

originalEvidenceClaims.statement: Restoring volume can suppress antidiuresis and produce water diuresis that accelerates sodium correction.
originalEvidenceClaims.limitation: Single guideline; observed urine/sodium trajectory establishes risk more directly than a fixed prediction.
originalEvidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

originalEvidenceClaims.statement: Malnutrition and hypokalaemia increase osmotic-demyelination risk; high-risk correction exceeding 8 mmol/L in a day warrants urgent reassessment.
originalEvidenceClaims.limitation: Guideline correction limits differ by risk group. No universal target or day-two limit inferred.
originalEvidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

originalEvidenceClaims.statement: Established excessive correction may require stopping correction-driving treatment and specialist-directed electrolyte-free water and desmopressin.
originalEvidenceClaims.limitation: Single adequate guideline, very-low-certainty desmopressin evidence. Reactive rescue is distinguished from disputed proactive clamp use.
originalEvidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

originalEvidenceClaims.statement: SIAD assessment requires hypotonicity with incompletely diluted urine, appropriate volume context and exclusion of adrenal, thyroid, renal and diuretic explanations.
originalEvidenceClaims.limitation: Single guideline; no diagnosis from urine sodium alone.
originalEvidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

originalEvidenceClaims.statement: Water restriction is a usual initial treatment of stable SIAD without severe neurologic symptoms.
originalEvidenceClaims.limitation: No exact fluid allowance or second-line drug ranking; guideline disagreement about vaptans is withheld.
originalEvidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

originalEvidenceClaims.statement: An indirect sodium method can underestimate sodium in a high-solids sample; direct ISE testing helps resolve this interference.
originalEvidenceClaims.limitation: One targeted laboratory review; the constructed lipid result is not an empirical interference threshold.
originalEvidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

originalEvidenceClaims.statement: Hypotensive hypernatraemic patients may first require isotonic crystalloid to restore circulation before a separate water-deficit plan.
originalEvidenceClaims.limitation: Narrative review plus older government guidance; no bolus size or correction speed is asserted.
originalEvidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

originalEvidenceClaims.statement: Measured urinary electrolyte-free-water loss can be estimated as urine volume * [1 - (urine sodium + urine potassium)/plasma sodium].
originalEvidenceClaims.limitation: One narrative review; retrospective measured estimate, not a prospective pump prescription. Include insensible/extrarenal losses separately.
originalEvidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

originalEvidenceClaims.statement: Ongoing renal water losses must be considered separately from the initial water deficit when planning hypernatraemia replacement.
originalEvidenceClaims.limitation: Single adequate review; future losses change and require reassessment. No precise correction-rate rule.
originalEvidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

originalEvidenceClaims.statement: Gastric acid losses can produce volume-depleted metabolic alkalosis with low urine chloride even when urinary sodium is higher.
originalEvidenceClaims.limitation: Single physiology review; urine chloride is interpreted before diuretics and saline alter the result.
originalEvidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

originalEvidenceClaims.statement: Volume- and chloride-depleted metabolic alkalosis is treated with chloride-containing volume replacement and potassium chloride.
originalEvidenceClaims.limitation: No exact dose/rate; treat the source of loss separately. Disease-specific obstruction management is outside this node.
originalEvidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

originalEvidenceClaims.statement: Magnesium deficiency can sustain potassium wasting and an inadequate potassium-replacement response.
originalEvidenceClaims.limitation: Government guidance corroborates checking/replacing magnesium in resistant hypokalaemia; no fixed replacement dose.
originalEvidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

originalEvidenceClaims.statement: Marked symptomatic magnesium depletion may require monitored IV magnesium, with caution about repeated dosing during renal impairment.
originalEvidenceClaims.limitation: One government source; no universal threshold, dose or infusion rate is taught.
originalEvidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

originalEvidenceClaims.statement: Fluid reassessment includes oral/enteral intake and medication-carrier fluids; overload should prompt review of ongoing sodium and water administration.
originalEvidenceClaims.limitation: Single older government guidance; not a diuretic or renal replacement indication and not a weight-based maintenance formula.
originalEvidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

originalEvidenceClaims.statement: In the 2024 adult DKA consensus, potassium below 3.5 mmol/L warrants replacement before insulin; insulin is delayed until potassium rises above 3.5 mmol/L.
originalEvidenceClaims.limitation: Single current multi-society consensus. Older pathways may use a different threshold; do not merge cutoffs.
originalEvidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

originalEvidenceClaims.statement: The consensus defines DKA resolution by blood ketones below 0.6 mmol/L plus venous pH at least 7.3 or bicarbonate at least 18 mmol/L.
originalEvidenceClaims.limitation: Single consensus; the AND/OR relation matters. Glucose and electrolyte monitoring remain necessary.
originalEvidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

originalEvidenceClaims.statement: Hyperchloraemic acidosis and persistent urinary ketones can outlast ketone clearance; neither anion gap nor urine ketones alone should define DKA resolution.
originalEvidenceClaims.limitation: Urinary acetoacetate can increase as beta-hydroxybutyrate falls. No claim that every low bicarbonate after DKA is benign.
originalEvidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

originalEvidenceClaims.statement: Transition from IV to subcutaneous insulin after resolution requires overlap to avoid an insulin-free interval.
originalEvidenceClaims.limitation: Single consensus; no dose or exact overlap duration is authored. Intake and prior basal insulin must be known.
originalEvidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

originalEvidenceClaims.statement: Falling glucose does not establish DKA resolution; dextrose permits continued insulin when ketone acidosis persists.
originalEvidenceClaims.limitation: Corroboration for historical frozen B2B30 only; no rewrite or new approval of it.
originalEvidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

originalEvidenceClaims.statement: During HHS treatment sodium can rise as glucose falls; fluid changes should consider osmolality and volume response rather than sodium direction alone.
originalEvidenceClaims.limitation: Single consensus; hypotonic saline is considered when osmolality fails to fall despite adequate balance. No exact infusion rate is authored.
originalEvidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

originalEvidenceClaims.statement: Ionized calcium reflects physiologically active calcium; total or albumin-adjusted calcium may not reliably represent it.
originalEvidenceClaims.limitation: Single government source; do not replace measurement with a new correction formula.
originalEvidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

originalEvidenceClaims.statement: Prolonged air exposure can lower a gas sample PCO2, raise pH and reduce measured ionized calcium through increased protein binding.
originalEvidenceClaims.limitation: One preanalytical review; no exact exposure-time or calcium-change formula claimed.
originalEvidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

originalEvidenceClaims.statement: Symptomatic substantial hypocalcaemia can require monitored IV calcium gluconate rather than waiting for oral correction.
originalEvidenceClaims.limitation: One government source; no exact drug dose, administration rate or extravasation technique authored.
originalEvidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified outside-hospital record; clinic presentation is retrospective.

originalEvidenceClaims.statement: Oral sodium chloride with a loop diuretic is one possible later-line SIAD approach after the initial water strategy.
originalEvidenceClaims.limitation: Single guideline; no universal ranking against urea or vaptans and no dose taught.
originalEvidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified constructed outside-hospital record.

originalEvidenceClaims.statement: Acetazolamide promotes bicarbonate excretion but may increase potassium loss; volume/chloride depletion should be addressed in chloride-responsive alkalosis.
originalEvidenceClaims.limitation: Narrative review; no fixed dose or universal use in volume-expanded patients.
originalEvidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified constructed outside-hospital record.

originalEvidenceClaims.statement: Routine bicarbonate is not recommended in DKA; the 2024 consensus permits consideration when pH is below 7.0.
originalEvidenceClaims.limitation: Single consensus; no bicarbonate dose or universal prescription authored.
originalEvidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified constructed outside-hospital record.

originalEvidenceClaims.statement: A basal-bolus subcutaneous regimen is preferred when transitioning suitable adults off IV insulin after DKA resolution.
originalEvidenceClaims.limitation: Single consensus; regimen depends on prior therapy, intake and clinical course. No correction-scale-only equivalence is inferred.
originalEvidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the specified constructed outside-hospital record.

originalEvidenceClaims.statement: Urinary acidification studies are reserved for selected unexplained metabolic acidosis without unmeasured anions, with urine pH directed by suspicion of tubular acidosis.
originalEvidenceClaims.limitation: R1.6-R1.7 are expert opinion; no urinary anion-gap formula or diagnostic cutoff is taught.
originalEvidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing the specified cause-directed acid-base evaluation.

sourceRechecks.finding: Diuretics confound urinary sodium interpretation. Risk-based correction/relowering remains individualized; poor intake for four days is not called malnutrition.

sourceRechecks.finding: Potassium must exceed 3.5 before insulin. The HHS glucose decline ceiling is 5-6.7 mmol/L/hour and the recommended osmolality decline is 3-8 mOsm/kg/hour. The constructed revision uses glucose fall 4 and osmolality fall 3 per hour; composition is assessed separately from rate.
